bug_semantics: GuardDog's default human-readable scan output concatenates attacker-controlled package identifiers, finding messages, file locations, and matched code snippets into the terminal without stripping or escaping C0/C1 control characters (including ESC). A malicious package can therefore place ANSI or OSC sequences in a filename (for example a name containing ESC[2J) or in source lines that the scanner matches; Analyzer._format_semgrep_response stores those values as {location, code, message} and HumanReadableReporter.print_scan_results (originally cli.print_scan_results) prints them raw via finding['message'] + finding['location'] + format_code_line_for_output(finding['code']). An analyst TTY or CI log may then clear/rewrite the screen, spoof log lines, or emit OSC 8 hyperlinks. JSON/SARIF reporters are out of scope; the injection is the unsanitized human-readable sink (CWE-116). GHSA/CVE list pip guarddog >=2.6.0,<=2.9.0, the HumanReadableReporter-module window; the same print sink already existed in CLI output from v0.0.2.
flaw_origin: On 2022-11-07, single-parent commit fab6f964209154c40ad031d1e944ada34419b5e4 ('Reformat code to allow for a nice output') replaced pprint/json CLI emission with print_scan_results and format_code_line_for_output, which interpolate finding['message'], finding['location'], and finding['code'] with no control-character sanitization. The same commit changed Analyzer._format_semgrep_response from a {location: snippet} map into a list of {location, code, message} dicts taken from Semgrep extra.lines/path/message. Immediate parent f035c31c09f91926d38baceb5c3f77ddd4f273a9 still pprint'd the structured result (Python repr, so ESC is escaped) and wrote verify output as JSON; those parent trees contain neither print_scan_results nor the finding dict. The 2025-05-08 extraction be780e60f761b9799666a506a8bb743527f78874 (first tagged in v2.6.0) only moved the same unsanitized concatenation into HumanReadableReporter and is a refactor, not the BIC. The sink was closed on 2026-05-06 by ec0705814fa3ebb0bf1507df3f4751cad5d0dda5, which added _TERMINAL_CONTROL_RE/_sanitize around identifier, message, location, and code, and shipped in v2.10.0.

reasoning: CVE-2026-44972 / GHSA-m5p4-gvpx-4mvr is a published CWE-116 terminal-escape issue, not withdrawn or rejected. The exploitable mechanism is unsanitized interpolation of package-controlled finding fields into default human-readable CLI output. That printer and the {location,code,message} formatter were first written together in fab6f964 on 2022-11-07; the immediate parent still used pprint/JSON and a different formatter shape, verified by parent-tree grep. Later be780e60 only relocated the same lines into guarddog/reporters/human_readable.py (the 2.6.0 surface the advisory cites) and is therefore not the BIC. The sanitizing fix ec070581 lands after v2.9.0 and is contained in v2.10.0, so BIC precedes the claimed affected range and the fix meets the patched boundary even though GHSA metadata still says no patched version. AI authorship was judged only from the BIC commit object: human Datadog author/committer, GPG signature, empty trailer set, no bot identity. Verdict is NOT_AI: real vulnerability, human BIC, known fix SHA.
